$comment: ONTOLOGY SCHEMA for the CV platform. Wired via
and checked by `ubc check` / `ubc schema validate` and by the sphinx-needs build.
Taken over from the BMS (rollout-demo-bms docs/schemas.json) with the same
structure and severity split (B§4.4): id prefixes, upward traces and field
presence are `violation`, reverse coverage and single-parent conventions are
`warning` (a backward obligation is owed by a later stage). `OBSERVED` in a
message refers to the BMS census the rule was derived from.
* every rule selects LOCAL needs only (`is_external == false`): imported
BMS_* needs are validated by the BMS, not re-validated here;
* test_result and gap carry the `product` they were produced for;
* allocates (CV arch -> BMS requirement) targets BMS interface needs only.
sphinx-needs needs the array form with `items` for `contains` on list
* the BMS black-box elements have their own type `bms_block` (produced by
stage bms_allocation): they satisfy a req and allocate BMS interface needs
and are not refined by CV swreqs (V§5 #8).

schemas.message: DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives user_story the prefix US_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives req the prefix REQ_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives arch the prefix ARCH_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives bms_block the prefix BB_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives swreq the prefix SWREQ_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives impl the prefix IMPL_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives test the prefix TEST_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives test_result the prefix TRES_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives risk the prefix RISK_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives decision the prefix DEC_.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives gap the prefix GAP_.
DECLARED (stage `reqs`, trace link=traces_to min=1 up=user_story): every req must trace up to a user_story. OBSERVED in the BMS.

DECLARED (stage `archs`, trace link=satisfies min=1 up=req): every arch must satisfy at least one req. OBSERVED in the BMS, fan-out 1..4 -- the upper end is left unbounded, an observed maximum is not a rule.
DECLARED (stage `bms_allocation`, trace link=satisfies min=1 up=req): every BMS black box must satisfy at least one req.
DECLARED (stage `swreqs`, trace link=refines min=1 up=arch): every swreq must refine an arch. OBSERVED in the BMS.
DECLARED (stage `code`, trace link=implements min=1 up=swreq): every impl marker must implement a swreq. OBSERVED in the BMS.
DECLARED (stage `tests`, trace link=verifies min=1 up=swreq): every test marker must verify a swreq. OBSERVED in the BMS.

DECLARED (stage `test_results`, trace link=results_for min=1 up=test) plus a STRUCTURAL upper bound: one recorded outcome belongs to exactly one test case in exactly one run, so a second target would make the evidence unattributable. Both bounds are violations, so they share one rule. OBSERVED in the BMS, all exactly 1.
DECLARED (stage `risks`, trace link=mitigates min=1 up=req): every risk must bear on at least one req. OBSERVED in the BMS, fan-out 1..2, upper end left unbounded.
DECLARED (stage `decisions`, trace link=affects min=1 up=arch): every decision must constrain at least one arch. OBSERVED in the BMS, fan-out 1..2, upper end left unbounded.

OBSERVED in the BMS: an imported gap must attribute itself to exactly one need. No `items` type test, because a gap can legitimately be raised against any type. `gap_for` is deliberately named by no stage trace edge -- an obligation to carry a gap would make a clean graph fail the gap gate -- so this rule only checks the shape the importer writes.

DECLARED (stage `reqs`, direction=both): every user_story must be decomposed into at least one req. OBSERVED in the BMS, fan-in 1..7. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS A VIOLATION, BACKWARD IS A WARNING note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `swreqs`, direction=both): every arch must be refined by at least one swreq, so no component is left without stated behaviour. OBSERVED in the BMS, fan-in 1..4. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS A VIOLATION, BACKWARD IS A WARNING note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `code`, direction=both): every swreq must be implemented. OBSERVED in the BMS, exactly one impl each. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS A VIOLATION, BACKWARD IS A WARNING note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `tests`, direction=both): every swreq must be verified. OBSERVED in the BMS, fan-in 1..3. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS A VIOLATION, BACKWARD IS A WARNING note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `archs`, direction=both): every req should be satisfied by at least one arch. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by the `archs` stage, which by construction runs after `reqs`, so a req authored before its architecture exists is exactly where the workflow expects it to be -- see the FORWARD IS A VIOLATION, BACKWARD IS A WARNING note in $defs._readme. The finding is `ubc agent gaps`'s to own; it reports it as a tracked gap need and points `ubc agent next` at the stage that owes the work. Not carved out by id either: a carve-out would need `not` in `select`, which sphinx-needs rejects, and an id-free carve-out would silently stop checking whole streams. CV: a BMS black box (bms_block) satisfies a req as well.

OBSERVED in the BMS: a req traces to exactly one user_story. Convention, not declared config -- a req that genuinely serves two stories is a design smell worth a second look, not an error. Kept separate from trace-req-traces_to because that rule's lower bound is declared and this upper bound is not.
OBSERVED in the BMS, and stated in ubproject.toml: a swreq refines THE arch element whose behaviour it pins down -- singular. Two parents means the behaviour belongs to neither component cleanly.
OBSERVED in the BMS: one impl marker realises one swreq. The one-line marker grammar accepts a list, so this is a convention the grammar does not enforce.
OBSERVED in the BMS: one test marker covers one swreq. A test asserting against two requirements at once is hard to attribute when it fails.

OBSERVED in the BMS: tools/import_test_results.py stamps outcome, runtime_s, test_run_label and chain_reqs on every generated result. Fields are global in ubCode and default to "", so this checks they were actually POPULATED, not merely present -- an empty one means the importer half-wrote the need. NOTE THAT NON-EMPTY IS ALL THIS RULE HAS TO SAY, even for the two fields that have a vocabulary: `[needs.fields]` already admits exactly `"" | <the valid values>` for both, so excluding "" here yields the valid values without this file restating them. outcome becomes exactly `passed | failed | error | skipped`, and test_run_label exactly the non-ISO timestamp form. Writing the enum out again would be a second copy to keep in sync, and the vocabulary belongs on the field because it holds for every need, not just this type. CV: also `product`, the product configuration the evidence was produced for (the importers run per product).

WARNING, NOT VIOLATION, ON PURPOSE. These are the seven categories the 0.34 engine emits, per CATEGORIES in tools/import_gaps.py -- but that importer renders an UNKNOWN category generically rather than rejecting it, because `ubc agent` is alpha and "a gate finding must never be dropped because this table has not caught up with the engine". A violation here would invert that: a newer engine emitting an eighth category would fail the build instead of reporting the gap. At `warning` the drift is surfaced -- go add the new category to CATEGORIES and to this list -- while the finding still lands. This is also why `[needs.fields.gap_category]` in ubproject.toml carries no global enum.

OBSERVED in the BMS: tools/import_gaps.py stamps gap_category, gap_need_id and gap_need_type on every generated gap. gap_need_id duplicates the gap_for link on purpose -- a report template cannot walk links, so the field is the half a Jinja report can read. CV: also `product`, the product configuration the evidence was produced for (the importers run per product).

PRESENCE only -- the VALUE is constrained globally by `[needs.fields.status]` in ubproject.toml (enum draft/review/approved), which is the right home for it because the vocabulary is the same wherever a status appears. This rule adds the half a global schema cannot express: WHICH TYPES OWE ONE. All 70 authored spec needs (user_story, req, arch, swreq, risk, decision) carry a status; the four derived types (impl, test, test_result, gap) carry none, correctly -- their state is the source file or the import, not a lifecycle -- and `status` is nullable precisely so they can. Raised from warning to violation now that the vocabulary is declared: a spec need with no status is no longer an unwritten convention.
CV (B§4.4): allocates may only target BMS requirements (BMS_REQ_*).
CV (B§4.4, B§5.2.3): allocates may only target BMS interface needs (tag `interface`).
CV (B§4.4): every BMS black box (bms_block) allocates at least one BMS interface need.
